claims.statement: The 23 `admin_*` endpoints are one repeated CRUD cycle applied to seven entities: a per-entity list screen that forwards to a list JSP, an edit screen whose request carries only the id and which is filled by `t2p()`, and add/update/delete handlers that delegate to an injected service and leave through a redirect result back to a list.

Back-office verb coverage is uneven: `category`, `property` and `product` expose all five verbs (list, add, edit, update, delete), `productImage` exposes list/add/delete, `propertyValue` only edit/update, `user` only list, and `order` list plus delivery — so no admin screen creates, edits or deletes a user, and orders have no admin create/edit/delete.

Every list action except `ProductImageAction.list` follows the same sequence: create a default `Page` when the request did not bind one, set its total from a service, set `page.param` with the parent key when the list is parent-scoped, load the collection, and call `t2p(parent)` when the shell needs a populated parent.

The parent key of a parent-scoped list request is load-bearing rather than optional: `PropertyAction.list` and `ProductAction.list` call `category.getId()` while building `page.param`, so a request without `category.id` fails instead of showing an unscoped list, and `adminPage.jsp` appends `${page.param}` to every pagination link so later pages stay inside the same parent.

All five back-office `...Page` results are `type="redirect"` results declared in the single `@Results` block on `Action4Result` and reused by every write handler: `listCategoryPage` to `/admin_category_list`, `listPropertyPage` to `/admin_property_list?category.id=${property.category.id}`, `listProductPage` to `/admin_product_list?category.id=${product.category.id}`, `listProductImagePage` to `/admin_productImage_list?product.id=${productImage.product.id}`, and `listOrderPage` to `/admin_order_list`.

Because a redirect location is evaluated as OGNL against the acting action instance before the URL is built, every association dereferenced in such a location must already be populated: the property, product and productImage add/edit forms carry the parent key in hidden inputs (`property.category.id` on the property screens, `product.category.id` on the product screens, `productImage.product.id` on the image screens), delete handlers call `t2p()` first, and the `ProductImageAction.delete` comment records that omitting the conversion raises `TransientObjectException` for `${productImage.product.id}`.

`t2p(Object)` converts the id-only entity bound by OGNL into a persistent row by reading the id reflectively, fetching the row through the injected `categoryService.get(clazz, id)`, resolving the setter named `set` plus the entity's simple class name on the runtime action class, and invoking it on the action itself — so the action's field, not the argument, ends up pointing at the row.

`t2p()` has 21 call sites overall, 12 of them on back-office screens: `CategoryAction.edit`; `PropertyAction.list`, `delete` and `edit`; `ProductAction.list`, `delete` and `edit`; `ProductImageAction.list` and `delete`; `PropertyValueAction.edit` and `update`; and `OrderAction.delivery`.

`t2p()` catches `Exception` and only calls `e.printStackTrace()`, returns `void` and defines no error result, so a failed conversion — missing row, failed `Integer` cast, or a non-public setter — is indistinguishable from success to the caller: the field keeps its previous value and the action still returns its result name, surfacing later either as a blank edit form or as the `NullPointerException` of a subsequent dereference.

Which write handler calls `t2p()` is decided case by case by what it needs downstream rather than by a rule: among delete handlers it is called for `property`, `product` and `productImage` but not for `category`; among update handlers only `propertyValue` calls it; and no add handler calls it.

`PropertyValueAction.update` stores the submitted `propertyValue.getValue()` in a local variable, then calls `t2p(propertyValue)`, then writes the stored value back onto the refreshed entity; the source comment states the ordering is required because `t2p()` replaces the bound object with the database row. 【人工评审待确认】 whether that order is intended design or a workaround for `t2p()`'s replace-the-field behaviour.

`admin_propertyValue_edit` is scoped by `product.id` rather than by a property-value id: the handler converts the product, calls `propertyValueService.init(product)` to insert a row for each property of the product's category that lacks one, and lists the product's values; `editPropertyValue.jsp` renders one text input per row with no form element and no submit button.

`admin_propertyValue_update` is driven by an AJAX `$.post` on every `keyup` of a value input, sending `propertyValue.value` and `propertyValue.id` and comparing the response body to the literal `success`; the handler returns the `success.jsp` result, a forward to `/success.jsp`, whose body is exactly `success`.

Every admin form field name is an OGNL property path on the `Action4Pojo` binding surface — `category.name`; `property.name` with its hidden `property.category.id`; `product.name`, `product.subTitle`, `product.remark`, `product.originalPrice`, `product.promotePrice`, `product.stock` with the hidden `product.category.id`; `productImage.type` with its hidden `productImage.product.id` — with the upload bound as `img`, and each edit form adds hidden inputs for the entity id and its parent key because the update handler's redirect needs them.

The back office is ten JSP shells under `web/admin/` (six list, four edit) that each declare their own page directive and taglibs and include the shared fragments under `web/include/admin/`: `adminHeader.jsp` (the `<!DOCTYPE html>` and `<html><head>` opening, jQuery 2.0.0 and Bootstrap 3.3.6 resource loads, and the `checkEmpty` / `checkNumber` / `checkInt` plus `deleteLink` confirmation helpers), `adminNavigator.jsp` (links to the three root lists), `adminPage.jsp` (pagination) and `adminFooter.jsp`.

Pagination reaches five of the six list shells through `adminPage.jsp`, but `listProductImage.jsp` has no pagination block because `ProductImageAction.list` never creates a `Page` and renders both image tables in full; the four edit shells omit `adminFooter.jsp`, so their documents are never closed — `editProduct.jsp`, for example, ends at the closing `` of its container on its last line instead of including the footer.

Back-office input validation and delete confirmation are client-side only: `adminHeader.jsp` defines `checkEmpty`, `checkNumber`, `checkInt` and an `a.click` handler that reads the `deleteLink` attribute, each shell wires those helpers into its own form's submit handler, and no action method validates the submitted values.

`PropertyAction.add` carries a method-level `@Transactional(readOnly = false)` although action instances are Struts-created and are not Spring beans, so no proxy can apply the annotation; the write is transactional anyway because `ServiceDelegateDAO.update/save/delete` and `BaseServiceImpl.save` are annotated themselves. 【人工评审待确认】 whether the annotation was meant to affect anything.

The product write path compensates for a server-owned field the browser cannot supply: `admin_product_add` stamps `createDate` with `new Date()`, and `admin_product_update` reloads the row first in order to copy the unchanged `createDate` onto the bound object that the edit form submitted — a form whose six bound scalars (`product.name`, `product.subTitle`, `product.remark`, `product.originalPrice`, `product.promotePrice`, `product.stock`) contain no date input.

The create flows persist the row before writing the file whose name is the id Hibernate assigned during that save, so the database write and the file write are not atomic: `CategoryAction.add` writes `img/category/<id>.jpg` unconditionally while `CategoryAction.update` guards the same call with `if (img != null)`, and `ProductImageAction.add` writes under `img/productSingle` or `img/productDetail` according to the posted `productImage.type`, deriving the small and middle single-image sizes.

Two admin handlers call a service that does not match the entity being handled: `ProductAction.list` computes its page total from `propertyService.total(category)`, so the number of pagination pages on the product list follows the category's property count, and `ProductImageAction.delete` deletes through `propertyService.delete(productImage)`; the delete still works because the base service's delete path is entity-agnostic.

No `admin_*` URL is authenticated: `AuthInterceptor`, the application's only auth check, acts only on request URIs starting with `/fore`, so all 23 back-office endpoints — every write and `admin_order_delivery` included — execute anonymously with no session user, role check or CSRF token, and the admin shells are plain JSPs under the web root that the descriptor protects with no security constraint. 【人工评审待确认】 whether anonymous back-office access is intended.

`remark` is bound through the same OGNL paths as the older product fields on all three product admin screens: the add panel's 备注 input is `name="product.remark"` placed directly after 产品小标题, the edit form echoes and re-posts it as `value="${product.remark}"` in the same position, and the list renders a 备注 column showing `${p.remark}` between 产品小标题 and 原价格.

`remark` is the one bound product field the client-side checks do not cover: neither the add shell's submit handler nor the edit shell's passes it to `checkEmpty`, while both check `name` and `subTitle`; because there is no server-side validation behind the handlers either, a `remark` value is written unchecked. 【人工评审待确认】 whether skipping `remark` is intended, given that the same handlers check `subTitle` and the new field is the only one they leave out.

Adding a new plain scalar to the product CRUD costs no action or service code: `remark` reaches the database purely through the OGNL binding onto `Action4Pojo.product` and `Product`'s ordinary mapped field with its unannotated getter/setter pair, `ProductAction` contains no remark-specific statement, and the column exists only because an `ALTER TABLE product ADD COLUMN remark varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL;` was appended to the seed script after the product INSERT block.
